target: Μην ανησυχείς, θα φτάσουμε στην ώρα μας.
english: Don't worry, we'll arrive on time.
tip: στην ώρα μας (stin óra mas) = on time — 'at our hour'.

english: I'm a little afraid of planes.
tip: φοβάμαι + thing directly (fováme) — no preposition needed.

english: I got really scared by the earthquake.
tip: Φοβήθηκα (fovíthika) = I got scared, one specific fright – the one-time past of φοβάμαι (fováme = I'm afraid). Greek splits one-off events from ongoing states in the verb itself.

english: I feel bad about yesterday.
tip: το χθεσινό (to chthesinó) = yesterday's thing — adjective used as a noun.

target: Ο μικρός ζηλεύει τη μεγάλη του αδερφή.
english: The little one is jealous of his big sister.
tip: ο μικρός (o mikrós) = the little one — article + adjective, no noun.

english: I missed you so much!
tip: μου έλειψες (mu élipses) = I missed you — 'you were missing to me'.

english: I don't think so, it's too expensive.
tip: Bare δεν νομίζω (den nomízo) = I don't think so.

english: I believe that too.
tip: το πιστεύω αυτό (to pistévo aftó) — the little το comes before the verb.

english: You're absolutely right!
tip: έχω δίκιο (écho díkio) = to be right — 'to have right'.

english: You're wrong, that's not what I said.
tip: κάνω λάθος (káno láthos) = to be wrong — 'to make error'.

target: Ας μη μαλώνουμε για το τίποτα.
english: Let's not fight over nothing.
tip: Ας (as) + verb = 'let's': ας μη μαλώνουμε (as mi malónume) = let's not fight. The μη(ν) (mi(n)) slots straight in for the negative – no extra 'do' or 'don't' machinery.

english: Okay, you have a point there.
tip: ένα δίκιο (éna díkio) = a point — partial agreement.

target: Μου αρέσουν τα βίντεο με ζώα.
english: I like animal videos.
tip: The liked thing is the subject, so plural things flip the verb: μου αρέσουν τα βίντεο (mu arésun ta vídeo) = the videos please me. One thing would take αρέσει (arési).

english: We like traveling together.
tip: A να (na) clause counts as one single thing, so it is always αρέσει (arési), never αρέσουν (arésun): μας αρέσει να ταξιδεύουμε (mas arési na taksiðévume) = traveling pleases us.

target: Μου άρεσαν όλα εκτός από το τέλος.
english: I liked everything except the ending.
tip: Past plural: μου άρεσαν (mu áresan) = I liked them.

target: Άρεσε σε όλους το φαγητό σου.
english: Everyone liked your food.
tip: When the liker is a noun, σε (se) marks them: άρεσε σε όλους (árese se ólus) = it pleased to everyone. The food is the subject – the people just receive the pleasing.

english: I like that you're always laughing.
tip: Μου αρέσει που γελάς (mu arési pu yelás) = I like that you laugh – που (pu) points at a real fact. Να (na) instead would mean liking the idea of laughing in general.

target: Ίσως πάμε Κρήτη φέτος το καλοκαίρι.
english: Maybe we'll go to Crete this summer.
tip: πάμε Κρήτη (páme Kríti) — destinations often drop 'to the'.

target: Είσαι σίγουρη ότι κλείδωσες την πόρτα;
english: Are you sure you locked the door?
tip: σίγουρος/σίγουρη (síguros/síguri) agrees with the person it describes — here 'you'.

target: Τι ωραία! Ήρθε επιτέλους η άνοιξη!
english: How lovely! Spring is finally here!
tip: τι + adjective = what a...: τι ωραία! (ti oréa) — no verb needed.

target: Μπράβο σου για τη νέα δουλειά!
english: Good for you on the new job!
tip: μπράβο σου (brávo su) = good for you — bravo takes 'your'.

english: No way! Kostas is getting married?
tip: τι λες! (ti les) = no way! — literally 'what are you saying'.

english: Finally! We waited an hour!
tip: επιτέλους (epitélus) = finally! — relief, not just 'in the end'.

english: What a day this has been!
tip: τι... κι αυτή (ti méra ki aftí) = what a day — exasperated flavor.

english: She was upset all day.
tip: στενοχωρημένος (stenochoriménos) = sad/upset — the -μένος 'in a state' form.

english: Calm down, nothing happened.
tip: δεν έγινε τίποτα (den éyine típota) = no harm done.

target: Στην αρχή φοβόμουν το αεροπλάνο, τώρα όχι.
english: At first I was afraid of flying, not anymore.
tip: φοβόμουν (fovómun) = I used to be afraid — ongoing past.

target: Το τέλος της ταινίας ήταν πολύ λυπητερό.
english: The end of the movie was very sad.
tip: Λυπητερό (lipiteró) = sad, for things like a movie's τέλος (télos = ending). Sad people are λυπημένοι (lipiméni) – Greek splits what causes sadness from who feels it.

target: Γελάσαμε πολύ με τα αστεία του θείου.
english: We laughed a lot at the uncle's jokes.
tip: γελάω με (yeláo me) = laugh AT — Greek says 'with'.

target: Αυτό το δωμάτιο είναι πιο φωτεινό.
english: This room is brighter.
tip: πιο + adjective = more: πιο φωτεινό (pio fotinó) = brighter. No ending change needed.
